topics.title: Stone Property Investment Overview
topics.summary: The discussion centers on the topic of stone property investments, exploring different facets and potential benefits associated with this type of real estate.

topics.title: Host Discusses Actor Complaints
topics.summary: The host expresses frustration with actors, particularly regarding their perceived arrogance and demanding behavior. He criticizes a young actor's dismissive attitude towards the host while discussing financial deals made for film appearances.

topics.title: Rock Stars, Mental Patients & Personal Annoyances
topics.summary: During a live broadcast, Howard Stern discussed rock musicians’ attention-seeking behavior alongside conversations about a party attendee named Shelly and her paranoia. He also addressed personal grievances like being snubbed by a typist, receiving an unusual gift from Sting, and the wack pack's internal conflicts.

topics.title: Musical Performances and Listener Calls
topics.summary: During the broadcast, a host discusses his fondness for his daughters while transitioning to musical selections including ‘Eleanor’ by The Turtles and ‘Revolution’ by Enough is Enough. He then takes calls from listeners who share opinions on these performances and relate personal experiences with music and relationships.

topics.title: Comic Book Convention & International Tensions
topics.summary: During a radio show, Howard Stern discusses comic book production details – cover artists, writers, and lettering specialists – while callers share anecdotes about their extensive collections, including one man with 5,000 rare comics. A segment shifts to concerns over potential French disengagement from international efforts regarding Iraq, fueled by rumors of the French seeking separate deals with Arab nations.

topics.title: Bush Freaks Over Letter, Kreskin Predicts War
topics.summary: During a discussion about potential war with Iraq, President George Bush reacts strongly to a letter from Secretary of State Baker to Saddam Hussein, expressing concern over communication difficulties and questioning his advisors’ judgment. Gary Kreskin then predicts the possibility of targeting Saddam himself if military action were taken.
